and 5011-5012 in fnn-owner-release-extents: `(serious-condition (e) (fnn-err "CHECKPOINT release failed (files stay retired): ~a" e))`. The block wraps fnn-log-make-durable (journal-directory fence), fnn-state-checkpoint-write (rename plus directory fsync, which raises fnn-indeterminate per io.lisp:2829-2830), fnn-log-drop, and the arena-mutating fn-xrt-reseat-checkpoint-frame (4971) inside a bare fnn-owner-gated.
fix: Narrow both handlers to the named refusals (fnn-store-io-refusal, the stop's yield refusal). Re-signal fnn-store-indeterminate and fnn-store-fault into a fenced owner quantum (fnn-owner-fault-service, or a stop at exit 3), and run the arena reseat through fnn-owner-shared-action-locked so a fault mid-reseat fences.

reviewer: owner.lisp:5127-5131: fnn-store-indeterminate from fnn-log-make-durable or fnn-state-checkpoint-write is logged as 'CHECKPOINT auto failed', and the serious-condition clause absorbs any fault, so serving continues with no fence. The reseat fault in fnn-owner-release-extents is swallowed the same way at 5011-5012. Partly mitigated: the checkpoint is derived state, durablep stays nil so nothing is dropped, and dir-pending stays set (io.lisp fnn-log-make-durable), so the commit path's first fence retries the journal/ fsync. That retry after an EIO can report success on Linux (fsync error consumed), so a later acknowledgement may rest on a directory entry that is not durable. This violates the rule that an ambiguous persistence failure is a recovery event.
scenario: The journal directory fsync in fnn-log-make-durable returns EIO, or the checkpoint rename lands and its directory fsync fails. Both are fnn-store-indeterminate, which AGENTS.md calls a recovery event. Here they are logged as 'CHECKPOINT auto failed' and the owner keeps accepting POSTs on a filesystem whose last fsync was lost. A digest mismatch while reseating a just-written frame (fnn-extent-fault, a store fault that must be exit 4) or an fnn-fault from a malformed ACL2 answer is swallowed the same way, possibly after some frames were reseated in the live arena and others were not.
title: Checkpoint publication and extent release swallow indeterminate fsync outcomes and store faults, then keep serving
